opportunities.title: Google Prompting Essentials: Online Learning Circle
opportunities.description: Ready to develop the skills to use generative AI (GenAI) tools effectively and responsibly for work and daily life? Join our staff-facilitated Learning Circle to complete the self-paced Google Prompting specialization. By completing this Learning Circle program, you will earn a Google Prompting Essentials certificate to share on your resume, LinkedIn and social media profiles! What You'll Learn This program is designed for those with some experience with using GenAI. Through short videos, articles, assignments and quizzes, you will discover: Essential Prompting Skills : How to use a prompting framework to create a desired output with GenAI; how to evaluate and refine your results. Everyday Work Tasks: Strategies to draft content, brainstorm ideas, create tables, timelines, and more. Data & Presentations: How to explore data visualization and use GenAI responsibly when working with data. Advanced Techniques: How to use prompt chaining for complex tasks and prompt versioning to save and reuse your best prompts over time. Learning Circles are study groups guided by library staff for people who want to complete the Google Prompting specialization together in a welcoming space: Learners meet weekly and work together through course materials. Participants are expected to commit to attending all four Learning Circle sessions. Some Experience with GenAI Recommended: This course is ideal for participants who have completed the AI Essentials course Learning Circle. How to Joi n a Learning Circle: Register once for the first session of this event series, in order to attend all sessions. Please sign up with a valid email address. A valid TPL library card is required for online circles. Attend all four sessions online via Zoom, on Tuesdays October 6, 13, 20, 27 from 1:30-4pm. Registration is a two-step process. First, participants must complete their registration through this page. After this step, library staff will follow up to request additional information in order to complete the registration. opportunities.title: Data Analytics Essentials Learning Circle
opportunities.description: Interested in learning about data analytics? Let's take a free online course together in a welcoming space! A learning circle is a study group, guided by library staff, for people who want to take a free online course together in a supportive and welcoming environment. Organizations all over the world recognize the value of analytics. Together, we'll learn about the essential tools used in this field. In this 12-week learning circle, we will work through the Data Analytics Essentials course from Cisco Networking Academy. We will explore the fundamental tools of a data analyst, including how to: transform, organize and visualize data with spreadsheet tools like Excel query data from a relational database using SQL improve data presentations using business intelligence tools like Tableau We will meet weekly, in-person, every Tuesday afternoon, September 15 - December 8, 2-3:30 PM (12 sessions). Participants are expected to commit to the duration of the course and attend sessions on a weekly basis. Learners who complete the course will be able to: earn a digital badge download a certificate of completion

opportunities.title: 5 Pieces of the AI Puzzle
opportunities.description: Presented by Keith McDonald, Founder of Toronto's the literacyAI project. A multi-media, interactive program demystifying artificial intelligence through an illuminating five-piece puzzle framework. This session guides participants toward a better understanding of AI's presence, clarifies confusion, and helps attendees navigate living, working, and playing alongside it. opportunities.title: Python Essentials 1 and 2 Learning Circle
opportunities.description: Learn Python and build your programming skills in a supportive group. This learning circle will meet on Tuesday afternoons from September 22 to December 8, 2-3:30pm. Learning circles are study groups guided by staff for people who want to take a free online course together in a welcoming space. Learners meet weekly and work together through the course materials. Participants are expected to commit to the duration of the course and attend all learning circle sessions. Learners who successfully complete both courses will earn a digital badge and certificate of completion. Python Essentials 1 is the first in a 2-course series that teaches computer programming skills including how to design, develop, and improve computer programs using the Python programming language. The course covers essential programming topics such as data types, variables, control flow, functions, and exceptions. Python Essentials 2 is the second in a 2-course series that will prepare you for the PCAP – Certified Associate in Python Programming certification exam at Pearson VUE. This intermediate-level course covers advanced aspects of Python programming, including modules, packages, exceptions, file processing and object-oriented programming (OOP). For more information about the Python learning circle, please contact networkingacademy@tpl.ca Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). opportunities.title: What is Artificial Intelligence?
opportunities.description: AI technologies have become increasingly prevalent in many aspects of modern life, including healthcare, finance, transportation, and entertainment. opportunities.title: Google AI Essentials: Online Learning Circle
opportunities.description: Curious about artificial intelligence or want to learn practical AI skills for work and personal use? Join our staff-facilitated learning circle to complete the self-paced Google AI Essentials specialization. This 10-hour introductory-level specialization, offered through Coursera, is available for free to learning circle participants. It is made up of five courses, each containing four units that consist of short videos, articles, assignments and a short multiple-choice quiz. By completing the specialization, you will learn: How AI works How to write effective prompts How to use generative AI tools responsibly How to identify AI's potential biases and avoid harm How to stay up to date with AI news After you complete the course, you earn a Google certificate and a badge to share with others Learning Circles are study groups guided by library staff for people who want to complete the Google AI Essentials specialization together in a welcoming space: Learners meet weekly and work together through course materials. Participants are expected to commit to attending all four learning circle sessions. No AI experience is required. How to Joi n a Learning Circle: Register once on the first session of this event series, in order to attend all sessions. Please sign up with a valid email address . opportunities.title: Colour & Atmosphere
opportunities.description: Join us for an online special career series with the 2026 Joanne Fitzgerald Illustrator in Residence , Elly MacKay! In this series, Elly will share insights into building a career in children’s book illustration, covering topics such as the journey to working as an illustrator, an overview of classic children’s books, portfolios, and colour. Details about each session follow: Thursday, October 8, 7pm: Becoming an Illustrator Elly MacKay shares her early and current work, her career path, and her process for creating miniature 3D worlds. Her talk also covers developing your style, illustration trends, and how to stand out. Thursday, October 15, 7pm: Looking at Picture Books Elly MacKay gives an overview of famous picture books, the various styles, what works, and how they’ve changed over the years. She looks at cover design, structure, page turns, and how visual storytelling and words work together. Thursday, October 22, 7pm: From Portfolio to Book Elly MacKay discusses portfolios and what to include, as well as working with agents and publishers. She also looks at what goes into creating your first picture book. Thursday, October 29, 7pm: Colour and Atmosphere Elly MacKay considers colour in picture books—how it can be used to strengthen a message, or to alter the mood. She looks at how illustrators have used colour in unconventional ways in their books. Workshops will be recorded and available for replay through Zoom until October 31, 2026. About Elly MacKay Elly MacKay is a children’s book author and illustrator and a paper artist. She studied printmaking and illustration at NSCAD University in Halifax and University of Canterbury in Christchurch. Elly creates miniature worlds with drawing, painting and cutting, and photographs them for illustrations in children’s books. She has more than 20 books published in Canada and the US, including The Enchanted Symphony by Julie Andrews and Emma Walton Hamilton, I Am a Meadow Mermaid and The Secret Fawn by Kallie George. Elly is both author and illustrator of Frostfire, In the Clouds and Red Sky at Night and others. She lives with her family in Owen Sound, Ontario. About the Joanne Fitzgerald Illustrator in Residence Program The Illustrator in Residence program honours the memory of illustrator Joanne Fitzgerald (1956-2011), and is a joint program of IBBY Canada, Toronto Public Library, and the Young Family. opportunities.title: Bring Your Problem: Can AI Help?
opportunities.description: Do you have a recurring problem you think AI might help with? A thing you keep doing by hand that feels like it should be easier? Bring it. If you don't have one, come help your neighbours with theirs. In this interactive class with our Innovator-in-Residence, Ryan Kelln , you'll learn a simple seven-step way to think about problems: what's annoying you, what you've tried, what AI could actually do, and where it would fail. We'll gather real problems from the room, sort them into groups, and map out what's worth solving with AI, and what's better solved without it. We'll also talk honestly about what an AI fix costs: your money, your time, and sometimes your private information. The problems AI could help with most are often the most personal, and the most personal ones are worth the most care. Registration is required and will start October 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM. opportunities.title: The Gravity Grand Prix
opportunities.description: Get ready to design, build, and race! This high-speed engineering challenge invites young adults (competing in teams of 2 ages 18-24) to design the ultimate gravity-powered race car. Using professional 3D modeling software and cutting-edge 3D printing technology, your team will compete to see who can conquer the downhill track the fastest. The core of this challenge is physics: maximizing kinetic energy while minimizing friction. How will you transform potential energy into pure speed?🛠️ The Challenge Rules The Software: All cars must be fully designed from scratch using OnShape. A brief Introduction to the software will be provided. The Material Limit: To keep the playing field level, your final race car is strictly limited to a maximum of 30 grams of 3D printed filament and 2 tooth picks. Free Prototyping: Failure is part of engineering! Teams are encouraged to print, test, and redesign. Prototype prints are completely free throughout the design phase. The Track: A straight, downhill gravity track built for maximum acceleration. 📅 Timeline & Important Dates Design & Prototyping Week: Nov 4 to Nov 11— Access the DIH, collaborate with your partner, and test your prototypes. Race Day: Nov 11 (Exactly one week after design week) — Family and friends are welcome to watch the final showdown! 💡 Key Engineering Focus Areas to take home the trophy, your team will need to think critically about: Aerodynamics & Friction: How will you reduce air resistance and wheel friction to keep your car gliding? Weight Distribution: How can you strategically place your 30-gram limit to maximize downward momentum?

opportunities.description: DIY Wooden Pneumatic Horse DIY Wooden Pneumatic Horse Kit teaches principles of air pressure and pneumatics to kids Ages 6 and up. Each child will get to take home one kit they build. DIY Wooden Pneumatic Horse Kit Engages children in practical activities Teaches principles of air pressure and pneumatics Includes all components for easy assembly Age: 5+ The DIY Wooden Pneumatic Horse Kit is an engaging and educational assembly kit designed specifically for children between the ages of 5 to 12. This kit offers children the opportunity to participate in practical activities, while simultaneously observing the movement of a wooden horse, propelled by the simple push and pull of a syringe. opportunities.description: Curious about artificial intelligence or want to learn practical AI skills for work and personal use? Join our staff-facilitated learning circle to complete the self-paced Google AI Essentials specialization. This 10-hour introductory-level specialization, offered through Coursera, is available for free to learning circle participants. It is made up of five courses, each containing four units that consist of short videos, articles, assignments and a short multiple-choice quiz. By completing the specialization, you will learn: How AI works How to write effective prompts How to use generative AI tools responsibly How to identify AI's potential biases and avoid harm How to stay up to date with AI news After you complete the course, you earn a Google certificate and a badge to share with others Learning Circles are study groups guided by library staff for people who want to complete the Google AI Essentials specialization together in a welcoming space: Learners meet weekly and work together through course materials. Participants are expected to commit to attending all four learning circle sessions. No AI experience is required. How to Join a Learning Circle: Register once on the first session of this event series, in order to attend all sessions. Please sign up with a valid email address . A valid TPL library card is required for online circles. Attend all four sessions in person at Northern District Library, Tuesdays November 3, 10, 17, and 24, from 6-8PM. This hands-on workshop introduces participants to the fundamentals of 3D design using Onshape, a cloud-based CAD software. Whether you're an aspiring engineer, designer, or hobbyist, this session provides the tools and knowledge to start creating your own 3D models. What You’ll Learn: Getting Started: Overview of Onshape's interface, navigation tools, and cloud-based collaboration features. Core Design Principles: Understanding 3D modeling basics, including sketches, extrusions, and revolutions. Best Practices: Tips for efficient modeling, managing design iterations, and exporting models for 3D printing or other applications. This program is ideal for beginners with no prior experience in CAD software, as well as those looking to explore Onshape's capabilities. Registration will start 2 weeks before this class. opportunities.description: Learn Python and build your programming skills in a supportive group. This learning circle will meet on Monday evenings from November 2 to December 7, 4-6pm. Learning circles are study groups guided by staff for people who want to take a free online course together in a welcoming space. Learners meet weekly and work together through the course materials. Participants are expected to commit to the duration of the course and attend all learning circle sessions. Used by startups and tech giants like Google, Facebook, Netflix, and more, Python offers you endless possibilities for creating small and large-scale software projects. User-friendly with easy-to-read code, Python is a great first programming language to learn and requires no prior programming knowledge. Python skills open you up to careers in almost any industry and are required if you want to continue to more advanced, higher paying software development and engineering roles such as software engineer, systems administrator, and security engineer. Python Essentials 1 In this course, you will learn in-demand skills such as how to design, develop, and improve computer programs, methods for analyzing problems using programming, programming best practices, and more. The course also prepares you for the PCEP – Certified Entry-Level Python Programmer certification (Exam PCEP-30-0x). opportunities.title: Bridging Minds: The Early Years (0 to 5): Small Actions, Big Impact
opportunities.description: Dr Aliza Israel and Dr Tatiana Valverde, child psychiatrists at Women’s College Hospital, will explore why the early years of life are so important for children's mental health, emotional well-being, and development. From birth to age five, children begin to develop the foundations for relationships, emotional regulation, learning, and resilience. Through everyday interactions, play, and nurturing relationships, parents, caregivers, and communities can help create a strong foundation for lifelong well-being. What to Expect: Understanding Early Childhood: Why the first five years are an important period for brain development, emotional growth, and lifelong mental health The Power of Relationships: How responsive caregiving, secure relationships, play, and everyday interactions help young children feel safe, connected, and supported Supporting Big Feelings: Understanding co-regulation and how parents and caregivers can help young children navigate big emotions, manage frustration, and gradually develop their own emotional regulation skills Small Actions, Lasting Impact: Practical, everyday ways families, caregivers, and communities can support children's mental health and help give every child a healthy start About the Presenters: Dr. Aliza Israel is a child and adolescent psychiatrist at Women's College Hospital, and lecturer at the University of Toronto in child psychiatry and women's mental health. Her work focuses on the interplay between maternal and child mental health, and in promoting resilience in young families. Dr. Israel lives in Toronto, Canada, with her husband and three rapidly-growing boys. She is also an amateur juggler who may or may not secretly wish to run away with the circus. Dr. Tatiana Valverde da Conceicao is a Child and Adolescent Psychiatrist at the Reproductive Life Stages Program at Women’s College Hospital. She’s an Assistant Professor at University of Toronto. Her clinical work involves general Child and Adolescent Psychiatry with a special focus on Early Childhood Mental Health. opportunities.title: Who Should Own AI? Building Public AI
opportunities.description: If AI becomes as important as roads, electricity, or libraries, who should own it? Who decides what it's used for? Who gets access and to say no? This panel discussion, as part of our Innovator-in-Residence program with Ryan Kelln , will include speakers building public-interest AI, working in civic tech, and organizing communities affected by AI decisions. We'll explore what's already being built, from open models and public compute to community-owned data, and what's being privatized. You'll get to draft your own "public AI requirements" and see what others think should be guaranteed to everyone. The future of AI is being decided now; this is a chance to have a say in it. opportunities.description: Saving the bees is an environmental cause that resonates deeply with Canadians. While most of us might not be thinking about bees this time of year, our actions during the colder months can still support these pollinators, particularly native bees, which are crucial and threatened by climate change, habitat loss, and other pressures. opportunities.title: From Screen Addiction to Self-Motivation: Ending the Daily Battle Over Video Games and Phones (**in Cantonese/Mandarin)
opportunities.description: Are daily struggles over gaming and phone use turning your home into a battleground? Do you feel caught between wanting high achievements for your children and feeling helpless against the pull of modern technology? You are not alone. In today’s digital age, traditional discipline methods often lead to constant power struggles, tears, and frustration for both parents and kids. Join Hopewoods Psychotherapy and Sparkling Seeds for a transformational, 1-hour parent workshop designed specifically for Chinese-speaking families navigating the digital world. What You Will Learn The Brain Behind the Screen (Neuroscience): Discover how dopamine and gaming design impact your child’s developing brain, and why simple restrictions or lectures often backfire. Connection Before Direction: Learn how to engage your child’s "upstairs brain" to manage emotional meltdowns and shift from conflict to co-regulation. Bridging Tradition and Attachment: Honour traditional parenting goals for discipline and success while deepening secure attachment and emotional trust. Fostering Self-Motivation: Transition from constant nagging and enforcement to helping your child cultivate intrinsic motivation and healthy self-control. __________________ Please note this workshop will be presented in Cantonese/Mandarin: 從螢幕成癮到自主動力 告別每日電玩與手機的拉鋸戰 每天為了手機和電子遊戲與孩子展開「攻防戰」，讓家裡變成戰場嗎？既希望孩子學業有成、有自律能力，又對無處不在的電子產品感到無力與焦慮？ 你並不孤單。在數位時代，傳統的強迫與管教方式往往只會引發不斷的權力鬥爭、眼淚與親子關係的撕裂。 誠邀您參加由 Hopewoods Psychotherapy 與 Sparkling Seeds 舉辦的 1 小時家長專題工作坊，專為華人家庭量身打造，帶您以全新的科學與心理學視角解開科技困局。 工作坊重點內容 螢幕背後的大腦機制（腦科學視角）： 了解多巴胺與遊戲機制如何影響孩子發育中的大腦，以及為什麼單純的強行禁止或說教往往適得其反。 先連結，後引導： 學習如何引導孩子的「上層大腦」，應對情緒失控，將親子衝突轉化為共同調節。 融合傳統期望與依附理論： 在尊重華人家庭對紀律與成就期望的同時，建立深層的安全依附與信任關係。 激發內在學習動力： 告別每日嘮叨與強迫，幫助孩子建立內在動機與健康的自我管理能力。 "當我們理解科技對大腦的影響，並以『依附關係』為導向時，我們不只是在減少螢幕使用時間，更是重塑與孩子終身受用的親子信任。"

opportunities.title: Journée pédagogique: Explorum - Bombes à bain
opportunities.description: L’expérience des bombes à bain est une expérience simple qui illustre une des réactions chimiques les plus communes : la neutralisation acidobasique qui forme un sel et de l'eau. Cette activité relaxante permet aux enfants de faire leur propre bombe à bain et de comprendre que cette réaction produit du gaz (des bulles) ; ils apprennent que l’acide contient du cations H+ et que la base contient des anions OH- qui réagissent ensemble pour former du sel et de l'eau. Chaque participant combine ses ingrédients et confectionne sa propre bombe à bain qu’il emporte avec lui emballée dans un petit sac en cellophane. The bath bomb experience is a simple activity that illustrates one of the most common chemical reactions: acid-base neutralization, which forms a salt and water. This relaxing activity allows children to create their own bath bomb and understand that this reaction produces gas (bubbles). They learn that the acid contains H+ ions and the base contains OH- ions, which react together to form salt and water. Each participant combines their ingredients and crafts their own bath bomb to take home, packaged in a small cellophane bag. opportunities.title: Tiny Titans: Insects Up Close | Book Launch & Panel Talk with Author & Photographer Dara Ojo
opportunities.description: Discover the hidden world of arthropods through stunning macro photography — a visual journey celebrating their beauty, complexity, and essential role in our ecosystems. Meet Dara Ojo , an award-winning macro photographer and conservation storyteller whose work brings the hidden world of arthropods into vivid relief. Ojo's book, Tiny Titans : The Silent Keepers of Our Ecosystem reveals the fascinating lives of insects, spiders, and other small creatures that quietly sustain life on Earth. Captured across Canada, Mexico, Costa Rica, and beyond, Dara Ojo’s photography highlights the intricate details and diversity of these often-overlooked species. Ojo will be leading the conversation with: Dr. Sandra Rehan , professor at York University and principal investigator of the Rehan Lab with a focus on wild bees, pollinator biology and conservation. Rehan's research explores the biology, behaviour and evolution of bees, with a particular interest in understanding and protecting native pollinators. Dr. Laura Timms , Senior Specialist of Natural Heritage Management at Credit Valley Conservation and Adjunct Professor with the Daniels Faculty’s Institute of Forestry and Conservation. Lorraine Johnson , author and native plant and ecological gardening advocate, bridging the connection between insects, plants, habitat and practical conservation action. Join in this evening to celebrate macro photography and the intricate beauty and ecological importance of insects and spiders, creatures that quietly anchor global biodiversity, pollination, and climate resilience. Free. Register for a reminder. 5:30 pm: Doors open. Mingle and chat with fellow nature and environmental enthusiasts! 6:00 pm: Presentation begins. Enjoy a highly visual presentation combining photography, science, conservation and storytelling, taking the audience behind the scenes of six years documenting tiny worlds across five continents and exploring why these overlooked species matter. A light, informal conversation with guest speakers will explore why arthropods are so essential to our ecosystems, with a discussion of challenges impacting local species, and how science, photography and art can work together to help people notice, understand and care about the natural world. An audience Q&A follows this discussion. 7:30 pm: Book signing with books available for purchase. *** This program is part of TPL's Our Fragile Planet program series, supported by Friends of Toronto Public Library, South Chapter.​ Questions? Please contact North York Central Library - Business, Science & Technology Department. *** Place a hold or borrow from Toronto Public Library: Tiny Titans : The Silent Keepers of Our Ecosystem (book) - Dara Ojo A Garden for the Rusty-patched Bumblebee (book) - Lorraine Johnson *** Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). opportunities.title: Learning Things You Love with AI
opportunities.description: Always wanted to learn to cook, draw, knit, fix a bike, or speak another language, but have trouble sticking to it? What if you had a personal AI tutor? In this class led by our Innovator-in-Residence, Ryan Kelln , learn how AI can become your personal tutor for something you love, or something new you want to fall in love with. A tutor explains things in the way you understand, asks you questions, and helps you choose what to learn next. Learn how to turn your goal into a specific, doable learning experiment: options not answers, with a practice that survives a bad day. Decide ahead of time how you'll know it's working: revise, or stop without guilt. You'll leave with a plan you actually want to try, and a sense for what AI should never decide for you. Prerequisites: Mouse, keyboarding and internet skills. Computers are provided. No coding experience required. Registration is required and will start November 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM. opportunities.description: Computers for Beginners 1: Use the Mouse A class on how to use a mouse for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience. In this fourth session you will: Understand how to read a web site address Practice using web addresses Search for information using a search engine Explore a web site in detail to understand its key components Upon completion of this class students will be able to use the internet at a beginner level and complete simple searches. Computers for Beginners 4: Use Google Search and Maps A class on using Google's filters, tools, and Maps for absolute beginners with little computer experience. In this fifth session you will: Use Google search tools more effectively to find websites, images, and news sites Explore Google Maps to find addresses and get directions for transit and road travel. Computers for Beginners 5: Use Windows A class on essential basic Windows skills for absolute beginners with little computer experience. opportunities.title: Shedding light on the dark side of the Universe
opportunities.description: The standard model of cosmology tells us that the Universe is mostly made up of ‘Dark Matter’, with normal matter contributing only about 15% of the total budget. However, direct detections have not yielded any results about the nature of this mysterious dark matter, leaving us with only indirect means of inferring its existence and distribution. I will try to answer tantalizing questions about its nature, and how it may have helped shape the Universe. This talk will be given by Dr. Pratika Dayal from the Dunlap Institute for Astronomy & Astrophysics at the University of Toronto. No registration is required, but registering will make sure you receive a reminder. opportunities.title: AI for Us: Shaping AI in Toronto
opportunities.description: Toronto is one of the biggest AI cities in the world. But what do the people here actually think about it and how do we want to shape its development and use? A panel of experts, alongside our Innovator-in-Residence Ryan Kelln , who know AI from very different angles, unite for an open conversation about what AI is doing to this city, and what we want it to do instead. We'll talk about: The human beings behind the machines: what drives the people who build AI, and what worries them. Work, money, and meaning: what happens to jobs, creativity, and value when AI lands here. Who gets to shape it and who's left out (both are our neighbours). The stories we tell: how art, media, news, and everyday talk shape what we expect, fear, and hope for. No pitches, no boosterism. Just an honest conversation about the ideas and stories shaping AI in this city, and what we want it to become. Featuring: Jerrold McGrath , Cultural Programmer and Theorist, In the Meantime Joseph Wilson , Anthropologist & Author of Humans of AI: Understanding the Humans Behind the Machines Owais Lightwala , Assistant Professor, Performance at The Creative School at Toronto Metropolitan University, Director, Chrysalis Registration is required and will start November 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM. Note: Your spot will not be guaranteed after 5 minutes of the start of the program. After this time, remaining seats will be filled on a first come, first serve basis until capacity is reached. opportunities.title: Peek Inside an AI Assistant: How It Thinks and Works
opportunities.description: You've asked an AI chatbot questions. But there's another kind of AI that doesn't just answer: it acts. In this demo-driven talk with our Innovator-in-Residence, Ryan Kelln , we'll look deeply at always-on personal AI assistants. The assistant can read your files, use your apps, and remember what you've told it, growing more useful over time. The same powers that let it help you can hurt you if something goes wrong. We'll also open up what happens inside: the hidden instructions, the tools it uses, what it remembers and forgets. Then we'll look at the AI assistant that helped develop this workshop, and how we shaped our workflow together, and why. Registration is required and will start November 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM. opportunities.title: Sven Beckert: A Global History of Capitalism
opportunities.description: TPL and Toronto Metropolitan University present historian Sven Beckert in conversation with Sanjay Ruparelia at the Toronto Reference Library's Appel Salon. As the Laird Bell Professor of History at Harvard University and co-chair of the university's Program on the Study of Capitalism, Sven Beckert has spent his career tracing how a single economic system came to structure nearly every aspect of modern life, how we work, how we think about ourselves and others, and how we organize our politics. In Capitalism: A Global History , Beckert reveals that capitalism was born global, corresponding at no point to an idealized dream of free markets; from the outset, state-backed institutions, imperial expansion, and coercion shaped its dynamics as much as innovation and exchange did. Along the way, capitalism has both expanded political voice for some and violently foreclosed it for others, entangled from its origins with slavery, colonialism, and profound inequality. How do we distinguish between capitalism's capacity to generate genuine prosperity and its tendency to concentrate power in ways that undermine democratic institutions? What can nearly a thousand years of capitalist history teach us about the conditions under which economic systems support, rather than erode, democratic life? And as we confront what many call a crisis of late-stage capitalism, what possibilities remain for reimagining an economic order more compatible with democratic values? Join one of the world's foremost historians of capitalism for an essential conversation about the deep entanglement of markets and democracy, and what history suggests about the road ahead. Question and answer session and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase. About this Event's Guests: Sven Beckert Sanjay Ruparelia Read More: Capitalism Empire of Cotton *** This event is part of our On Civil Society series, where we host local and international authors, activists and academics in conversation about the most critical topics of our time. Generously supported by the McConnell Foundation and also by Chris M. Reid. *** About the series: On the Frontlines of Democracy is a public lecture series to analyze the trajectory of democracy in the twenty-first century. In every region, the prospects of democracy face serious challenges, old and new. Can we protect constitutional rights and renew collective self-rule in an era of popular mistrust, severe partisanship and resurgent nationalism? Can they reduce inequalities of power, wealth and status, defend deep diversity and confront climate change in the new digital age? Can we develop innovative strategies to revitalize civic engagement, empower public institutions and resist autocratic threats? And what can we offer, learn and do to promote the prospects of democracy in our increasingly post-western global order? *** PLAN YOUR VISIT : Location: Bram and Bluma Appel Salon, Toronto Reference Library (789 Yonge Street), 2nd floor Time: Doors open 6:00 pm, Event starts 7 pm. Tickets: Free registration required. Ticket policy: Tickets guaranteed until 6:50 pm, after which rush line admission begins. Seating first come, first served. Bar: Beer/wine available for purchase (debit/credit only). TPL is committed to accessibility. If you are Deaf or have a disability and would like to request accommodation for this event, please contact accessibleservices@tpl.ca or 416-393-7099 at least three weeks prior to the event. *** Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). opportunities.title: AI At Home: No Cloud, No Account
opportunities.description: What if your AI didn't need the internet at all: no subscription, no one recording what you type? In this class led by our Innovator-in-Residence, Ryan Kelln , you'll see AI models running entirely on one computer, with no connection and no data leaving the room. opportunities.description: How does a machine actually "think"? Explore the history and latest developments of machine learning. In this class led by our Innovator-in-Residence, Ryan Kelln , we'll dig into what's really going on inside AI systems: how they decide what matters in your question, where their training data comes from (and who's missing from it), and how hidden instructions can sneak into content and hijack an AI. Develop an intuitive understanding of how AIs "think" without the math. We'll talk about how AIs remember, how they don't and how they are both similar and different to humans. opportunities.title: AI, Our Community and What Happens Next
opportunities.description: Twelve weeks of making, testing, and learning. Now what do we do with it? Join Innovator in Residence Ryan Kelln for his closing event, as he reflects on the Applied AI residency: the projects people built, the unexpected moments that taught us the most, and the needs we discovered but couldn't solve. We'll tell our stories. Then it's your turn. In small groups, we'll ask: what should we continue, what should we change? Help turn what we learned into commitments to the future: what this community could build and nurture together, in fruitful and responsible collaboration with AI. Registration is required and will start November 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM. Note: Your spot will not be guaranteed after 5 minutes of the start of the program. opportunities.title: Resilience Reads: a climate neighbourhood reading party
opportunities.description: Join us to share the joy of reading, while building climate resilience knowledge. Members are invited to discuss a book they are reading, tell stories, and empower each other to explore community-driven solutions. Each party will start with a quiet read and reflect time, with opportunities to join group discussions later on over refreshments. AUGUST – Fossil Fuel Folly American War by Omar El Akkad or your favourite dystopian read! or your favourite book featuring water! SEPTEMBER – We Need Pollinators The History of Bees by Maja Lunde or your favourite animal-centred book! OCTOBER – Climate Change is Scary The Annual Migration of Clouds by Premee Mohamed or a different book that shares a scary future ecological crisis! NOVEMBER - Climate Changes Everything Ministry for the Future by Kim Stanley Robinson or your favourite time travel read! Copies are available in the branch to pick up, while supplies last. Registration is encouraged but drop ins are welcome! opportunities.title: Resilience Reads: a climate neighbourhood reading party
opportunities.description: Join us to share the joy of reading, while building climate resilience knowledge. Members are invited to discuss a book they are reading, tell stories, and empower each other to explore community-driven solutions. Each party will start with a quiet read and reflect time, with opportunities to join group discussions later on over refreshments. AUGUST – Fossil Fuel Folly American War by Omar El Akkad or your favourite dystopian read! or your favourite book featuring water! SEPTEMBER – We Need Pollinators The History of Bees by Maja Lunde or your favourite animal-centred book! OCTOBER – Climate Change is Scary The Annual Migration of Clouds by Premee Mohamed or a different book that shares a scary future ecological crisis! NOVEMBER - Climate Changes Everything Ministry for the Future by Kim Stanley Robinson or your favourite time travel read! Copies are available in the branch to pick up, while supplies last. Registration is encouraged but drop ins are welcome! opportunities.description: Are you a homeschooler family? Markham Public Library hosts weekly meetups for homeschooler families on Monday mornings at the Angus Glen Library Branch from 10:30AM - 12:00PM . These meetups give participating caregivers and children an opportunity to connect with other homeschooling families, work together to explore various STEAM building and literacy development focused activities, learn about library resources, meet special guest speakers, and more! PLEASE NOTE: Adults (caregivers) are responsible for supervising and assisting the children in their care with all planned activities and/or exercises Most planned activities are suitable for ages 5+ and may be subject to change Active participation and engagement of all caregivers is required ⚠️ PLEASE REGISTER TO ATTEND: We require advance registration for this program due to limited space, room capacity, and to support the library in our ability to plan activities and prepare supplies. opportunities.title: Resilience Reads: a climate neighbourhood reading party
opportunities.description: Join us to share the joy of reading, while building climate resilience knowledge. Members are invited to discuss a book they are reading, tell stories, and empower each other to explore community-driven solutions. Each party will start with a quiet read and reflect time, with opportunities to join group discussions later on over refreshments. AUGUST – Fossil Fuel Folly American War by Omar El Akkad or your favourite dystopian read! or your favourite book featuring water! SEPTEMBER – We Need Pollinators The History of Bees by Maja Lunde or your favourite animal-centred book! OCTOBER – Climate Change is Scary The Annual Migration of Clouds by Premee Mohamed or a different book that shares a scary future ecological crisis! NOVEMBER - Climate Changes Everything Ministry for the Future by Kim Stanley Robinson or your favourite time travel read! Copies are available in the branch to pick up, while supplies last. Registration is encouraged but drop ins are welcome! opportunities.description: Are you a homeschooler family? Markham Public Library hosts weekly meetups for homeschooler families on Monday mornings at the Angus Glen Library Branch from 10:30AM - 12:00PM . These meetups give participating caregivers and children an opportunity to connect with other homeschooling families, work together to explore various STEAM building and literacy development focused activities, learn about library resources, meet special guest speakers, and more! PLEASE NOTE: Adults (caregivers) are responsible for supervising and assisting the children in their care with all planned activities and/or exercises Most planned activities are suitable for ages 5+ and may be subject to change Active participation and engagement of all caregivers is required ⚠️ PLEASE REGISTER TO ATTEND: We require advance registration for this program due to limited space, room capacity, and to support the library in our ability to plan activities and prepare supplies. We ask that all participants (caregivers and children) please sign-up for each session to guarantee your spot! *** ***For example, if there is 1 caregiver and 3 children attending, please indicate 4 in the registration.

opportunities.title: Resilience Reads: a climate neighbourhood reading party
opportunities.description: Join us to share the joy of reading, while building climate resilience knowledge. Members are invited to discuss a book they are reading, tell stories, and empower each other to explore community-driven solutions. Each party will start with a quiet read and reflect time, with opportunities to join group discussions later on over refreshments. AUGUST – Fossil Fuel Folly American War by Omar El Akkad or your favourite dystopian read! or your favourite book featuring water! SEPTEMBER – We Need Pollinators The History of Bees by Maja Lunde or your favourite animal-centred book! OCTOBER – Climate Change is Scary The Annual Migration of Clouds by Premee Mohamed or a different book that shares a scary future ecological crisis! NOVEMBER - Climate Changes Everything Ministry for the Future by Kim Stanley Robinson or your favourite time travel read! Copies are available in the branch to pick up, while supplies last. Registration is encouraged but drop ins are welcome! opportunities.title: Resilience Reads: a climate neighbourhood reading party
opportunities.description: Join us to share the joy of reading, while building climate resilience knowledge. Members are invited to discuss a book they are reading, tell stories, and empower each other to explore community-driven solutions. Each party will start with a quiet read and reflect time, with opportunities to join group discussions later on over refreshments. AUGUST – Fossil Fuel Folly American War by Omar El Akkad or your favourite dystopian read! or your favourite book featuring water! SEPTEMBER – We Need Pollinators The History of Bees by Maja Lunde or your favourite animal-centred book! OCTOBER – Climate Change is Scary The Annual Migration of Clouds by Premee Mohamed or a different book that shares a scary future ecological crisis! NOVEMBER - Climate Changes Everything Ministry for the Future by Kim Stanley Robinson or your favourite time travel read! Copies are available in the branch to pick up, while supplies last. Registration is encouraged but drop ins are welcome! opportunities.description: Looking for something to do after school? Come out to our After School Club and learn new things, make stuff, meet other kids and have fun! For ages [ 6-12.] Snacks are offered during the After School Club for participants. Ingredient lists will be available. Snacks are generously supported, in part, by donors.

opportunities.title: STEM Club
opportunities.description: Join us at the library for a fun hour of stem related activities. Come out to build, create and code with Snap Circuits, Dash and Dot, Scratch Coding, LEGO, Magnetic Tiles and more! The club is intended for children aged 6 to 12 years. Due to the limited number of robots, participants may be asked to share with other participants. Drop-in. No registration is required.
opportunities.address: Parliament Street, 269 Gerrard Street East, Toronto, ON, M5A 2G3

opportunities.title: STEAM Lab
opportunities.description: Join us for our weekly STEAM Lab (Ages 6-12) , where kids can explore science, technology, engineering, art, and math through fun, hands-on activities. From building simple robots and experimenting with Snap Circuits to creative design challenges and more, there’s always something new to discover. Activities change each week, so there’s always something new to explore!
opportunities.address: Hillcrest, 5801 Leslie Street, Toronto, ON, M2H 1J8
